title: Coroutines
summary: Independently pausable/resumable threads of execution (not parallel OS threads). In Roblox you usually want the task library instead — task.spawn/task.delay are coroutine-based and engine-integrated.

methods.name: coroutine.create
methods.description: Creates a new coroutine thread wrapping f, without starting it.

methods.name: coroutine.resume
methods.description: Starts or continues the coroutine, passing values to its yield points. First return is success; on failure the second is the error message.

methods.name: coroutine.yield
methods.description: Pauses the current coroutine, sending values back to the resumer.

methods.name: coroutine.wrap
methods.description: Returns a function that resumes a new coroutine on each call. Unlike resume, errors propagate directly.

methods.name: coroutine.isyieldable
methods.description: Whether the current context can yield.

methods.name: coroutine.close
methods.description: Luau addition. Closes a suspended coroutine, releasing it.

details.heading: Cooperative, not parallel
details.body: Coroutines run one at a time on the same core. They only switch at explicit yield/resume points (or engine yields like task.wait). They are for structuring control flow, not speed.

explanation.whatItIs: A coroutine is a function that can pause in the middle and be resumed later, keeping all its local state alive. Picture putting a bookmark in a function and coming back to it.
explanation.whyItExists: Roblox's entire script model is built on them: every event callback, every task.wait, every 'parallel-looking' behavior in a single-threaded engine is coroutine plumbing.
whenToUse: Understanding what the engine does under the hood (scripts, delays, waits)
Custom state machines that pause and resume
whenNotToUse: For day-to-day Roblox work, prefer `task.spawn`, `task.delay`, `task.defer` — they schedule onto the engine properly and report errors to Output
Never use raw coroutines for 'multithreading' — there is no parallelism here
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
co = coroutine.create(function()
    print("A")
    coroutine.yield()      -- bookmark here
    print("B")
end)

coroutine.resume(co)   --> prints A, pauses
coroutine.resume(co)   --> prints B, finishes
```
tips: Prefer the task library in Roblox — it's coroutines plus engine scheduling
`coroutine.wrap` hides the success flag; use resume when you need error info
commonMistakes: Assuming coroutines run simultaneously — they interleave only at yield points
Resuming a dead coroutine (returns false, 'cannot resume dead coroutine')
Using bare coroutine.create where task.spawn would integrate with the frame loop and error reporting

examples.title: Pause and resume
examples.code:
local co = coroutine.create(function(name)
    print("start", name)
    local extra = coroutine.yield()     -- pause; receive value on resume
    print("resumed with", extra)
end)

coroutine.resume(co, "worker")   --> start worker
coroutine.resume(co, 42)         --> resumed with 42

examples.title: Prefer the task library in Roblox
examples.code:
-- Instead of hand-rolled coroutines:
task.spawn(function()
    print("runs on its own thread")
end)

task.delay(2, function()
    print("two seconds later")
end)
examples.whyItWorks: task.spawn/task.delay create threads the engine schedules and tracks — with errors reported to Output — which is what you almost always wanted from coroutines.
